note: What kind of scene each photograph is, and therefore what the census is allowed to put in the shopper's bag. This is the label set for the subject gate in `normalizeCensusResponse`, which decides whether a census reaches the bag at all. Scored by `server/eval/pipeline/scene-gate.ts`.
why: The gate was written to stop a photograph of a shop's shelves from filling the bag with goods the shopper is not buying, and it does that correctly. It was written as one boolean, cart or not, so it also empties the bag for a shopper who holds a single product up to the camera, which is the interaction the product owner asked for on 2026-09-01: point the phone at a grocery item and have it added to the cart. Those are two different scenes and one boolean cannot separate them, so the label has three values.

kinds.cart: the inside of the shopper's own trolley or basket. Census everything, this is the original use case.
kinds.product: one or a few products the shopper is presenting to the camera, held up or set down on a surface. Census them: this is the shopper showing the app what they are buying.
kinds.shelf: retail shelving, a chiller, a display stand, another shopper's trolley, the floor. Name nothing. The goods are not theirs and must never reach the bag.

provenance: cart and shelf assignments are taken verbatim from `counts.json` in this folder, which states that IMG_0247, IMG_0248, IMG_0250 and IMG_0251 are store shelves and the other six are one trolley being loaded. The two practice stills are labelled here for the first time; `manifest.json` recorded them as unlabelled and described their contents, and those descriptions match what is in the files.
